summary: The study describes the use of atomic layer deposition (ALD) to deposit metallic Ru nanoparticles on the internal surfaces of carbon and silica aerogels. The process involves alternating exposures to Ru Cp2 and air at 350 ◦C, resulting in uniform metal loading and stable Ru nanoparticles. The technique allows for precise control over metal loading and particle size by adjusting the number of ALD cycles. The study also discusses the limitations of the ALD approach and suggests potential improvements.
evidence: We present a general approach to prepare metal/aerogel nanocomposites via template directed atomic layer deposition (ALD). In particular, we used a Ru ALD process consisting of alternating exposures to bis(cyclopentadienyl)ruthenium (Ru Cp2) and air at 350 ◦C to deposit metallic Ru nanoparticles on the internal surfaces of carbon and silica aerogels. The technique does not affect the morphology of the aerogel template and offers excellent control over metal loading by simply adjusting the number of ALD cycles.
